meta.title: He Sawed The Legs Off A Table In 1956. It Became IKEA's Entire Business Model.
meta.hook: In 1956, an IKEA designer sawed the legs off a table just to fit it in his car.
meta.description: In 1956, IKEA designer Gillis Lundgren couldn't fit a table into his Volvo, so he removed the legs and packed it flat. That accident became IKEA's core business model: ship furniture unassembled, let the customer build it, and fit far more product into every truck and container. It's how a Swedish catalog company grew into one of the largest furniture retailers in the world.

scenes.narration: In nineteen fifty-six, an IKEA designer sawed the legs off a table just to fit it in his car.

visual.query: wooden table legs sawn off workshop close up
visual.visual_intent: A wooden table leg being sawn off on a workshop bench, sawdust falling, harsh workshop light, close and tactile
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the literal accident, hard cut

scenes.narration: Staring at the pieces on the ground, he had an idea. What if furniture never left the factory fully assembled?

visual.query: disassembled furniture parts flat on floor
visual.visual_intent: Flat furniture panels and hardware laid out neatly on a floor, overhead shot, clean daylight
visual.decision_reason: the idea beat, calm after the accident

scenes.narration: Ingvar Kamprad turned that accident into IKEA's whole model: ship it flat, let the customer build it at home.

visual.query: flat pack furniture boxes warehouse stacked
visual.visual_intent: Rows of flat cardboard furniture boxes stacked on warehouse shelving, wide pan, industrial light

scenes.narration: Flat boxes stack tighter than finished furniture, so more product fits on every truck, every container, every store shelf.

visual.visual_intent: Shipping containers stacked densely at a cargo port, wide aerial-feeling shot, cool industrial light
visual.decision_reason: visualizes the packing-density advantage that drives the economics

scenes.narration: That shift moved the assembly labor onto the customer, in exchange for a dramatically lower price.

visual.visual_intent: A person kneeling on a living room floor assembling flat-pack furniture with an allen key, warm home light
visual.decision_reason: the customer's side of the trade

scenes.narration: It's why IKEA grew into one of the largest furniture retailers on Earth, built on a table that wouldn't fit in a car. Follow for more.
